sections.title: Core Foundations & Principles
sections.content:
• **Productivity Maintenance**: Enhances or sustains production/services, particularly primary productivity and food security.
• **Risk Reduction**: Reduces the level of production risk by improving the resilience of land against climatic shocks and soil erosion.
• **Resource Protection**: Prevents the degradation of soil and water quality through integrated watershed management and conservation tillage.

sections.title: Classification / Dimensions Matrix
rows: Contour farming, mulching, crop rotation, and minimum tillage.
Useful for Prelims match-the-following questions on climate-smart agriculture.
Terracing, check dams, contour bunds, and percolation tanks.
Core components of watershed development schemes like PMKSY-WDC in Mains.
Agroforestry, windbreaks, shelterbelts, and strip cropping.
Vital for tackling desertification under UNCCD COP targets.

items.definition: A state whereby the amount of healthy and productive land resources remains stable or increases over specified temporal and spatial scales under UNCCD.
Minimizing soil disturbance, maintaining organic soil cover, and practicing crop rotation to preserve soil microbiome and carbon sink capacity.

items.title: Mnemonic for SLM Core Pillars (SAVE)
items.content:
• **Formula / Acronym**: S - Soil health, A - Agroforestry integration, V - Vegetative cover, E - Economic viability.
• **How to Apply**: Instantly structure a 10-marker answer on 'Measures for Sustainable Land Management' in GS-3.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Confusing Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) with zero land degradation. LDN allows degradation in one area provided it is offset by restoration in another area to achieve net-zero change.
Prelims / Mains Tip: Always link SLM frameworks with co-benefits like climate change mitigation (UNFCCC) and biodiversity conservation (UNCBD) to show multidimensional analytical depth.

keyTakeaways: SLM integrates agronomic, structural, and vegetative methods to combat desertification.
Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is a key SDG 15 target for India by 2030.
Conservation agriculture and watershed management form the bedrock of sustainable rural livelihoods.
